issues.description: Constructor parameter order mismatch for class Meal: the problem statement UML and the solution implementation declare a constructor Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (name first, then ingredients). The template implementation declares the constructor with the parameters reversed: Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). The template's Main.java usage (new Meal("cowBoyStew", new String[]{...})) and the UML expect the (String, String[]) order. This discrepancy will cause compilation errors or confusion when students run the provided examples or follow the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in the template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and update the constructor body to assign this.name = name; this.ingredients = ingredients; so the parameter order matches the UML, the example usage in Main, and the solution. Alternatively (less preferred), update the problem statement UML and example usages to match the template, but modifying the template constructor is recommended to avoid breaking the provided examples.
